subject.title: feat(anthropic): enforce --safe-mode on all claude-cli subprocess launches

question: Should OpenClaw require Claude Code 2.1.169+ for the Anthropic CLI backend, or preserve compatibility with older installed Claude CLIs while applying safe mode only when supported?
rationale: The patch intentionally turns a Claude CLI capability into mandatory OpenClaw launch policy, but the repository evidence supplied does not establish that the stated Claude CLI minimum is already a supported product contract.

options.title: Use capability-compatible behavior
options.body: Apply safe mode only when the installed Claude CLI supports it and retain the current launch behavior otherwise, with a clear supported-version path.

options.title: Adopt a hard minimum
options.body: Make Claude Code 2.1.169+ an explicit Anthropic CLI backend requirement and provide a direct upgrade diagnostic before any subprocess launch.

options.title: Do not force the flag
options.body: Keep the existing configuration behavior if host-level Claude customization isolation is not an approved OpenClaw policy.

recommendation.title: Use capability-compatible behavior
recommendation.body: Apply safe mode only when the installed Claude CLI supports it and retain the current launch behavior otherwise, with a clear supported-version path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest evidence-backed contributor to the current Anthropic CLI argument-policy boundary.
